craft_notes: Sthāyin: ānanda-vīra of play; vyabhicāri exultant joy (ullāsa) at making-unmaking at once. Sanskrit-first: krīḍā-kautuka (PLAY-DELIGHT — kept dignified); yugapat (AT-ONCE — simultaneity kept); sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra (MAKINGS/UNMAKINGS — process nouns, not god-verbs). Rows: 9 (makings/unmakings pair + at-once), 8 (bright vowels throughout: eager/delight/makings — ānanda fills, no dark close), 1 (‘all-pervading’ closes — everywhere ends everywhere). Close: ‘the all-pervading’. Rupture: semicolon (mood turns to act — play-eager, therefore making). Rejected: ‘forever keen on fun’ — killed: dignity; ‘creates and destroys’ — killed: process nouns kept; ‘ frolics’ — killed: colloquial. Read aloud: THIS-god, WITH-this-GOD-dess, for-EV-er EA-ger FOR-play's de-LIGHT … VAR-ied MAK-ings AND-un-MAK-ings HE-works AT-once — THE-all-per-VAD-ing.

lines: This god, with this goddess, forever eager for play's delight;
varied makings and unmakings He works at once — the all-pervading.
l4.sanskrit_cite: eṣa devo 'nayā devyā nityaṃ krīḍārasotsukaḥ | vicitrān sṛṣṭisaṃhārān vidhatte yugapad vibhuḥ

c1_essence: Play-eager pair make-unmake varied worlds simultaneously, everywhere.
